title: Check: History of the Periodic Table (2)

questions.stem: What pattern did Newlands notice when he arranged elements by atomic mass?

options.text: Elements came in groups of three with similar properties
Every eighth element had similar properties, like musical octaves
All metals were heavier than non-metals
Elements alternated between metals and non-metals

questions.explanation: Newlands proposed his 'Law of Octaves' in 1864, noting that every eighth element had similar properties when arranged by atomic mass. However, this only worked up to calcium and failed for heavier elements, leading to ridicule from other scientists.

questions.stem: Mendeleev placed tellurium before iodine despite tellurium having a higher atomic mass. Why?

options.text: He made an error in his calculations
He did not know the atomic masses
He prioritised chemical properties over strict atomic mass order

questions.explanation: Mendeleev prioritised chemical properties over strict atomic mass order. Tellurium has properties similar to sulfur and selenium (Group 6), while iodine is similar to chlorine and bromine (Group 7). Swapping them ensured each element sat with elements of similar properties.
